note: Provider-review ending for a reported non-emergency red flag. Educational draft pending Deborah’s review. Not a diagnosis or a hormone-only explanation; no products or automatic wellness plan.
lead: Thank you for telling me. Please see a doctor within 24 hours, or on the first business day if it's the weekend. Here is how to prepare for that conversation.

sections.body: You reported: {concerns}. I hear your concern, and it is worth bringing directly to a healthcare professional.
The hypothalamus helps coordinate many body functions, but that does not establish a hormonal cause for what you reported. This conversation cannot determine the cause.
There can be different explanations. A provider can assess your history and the symptom itself; a general hormone-focused answer would not settle that question.
Questions you can bring to your provider:
bullets: How should the concern I reported be assessed?
What details about when it started and how it has changed would help you?
What changes should prompt me to seek more urgent help?

sections.body: Ask your provider whether an examination or any tests are appropriate. The choice depends on their assessment; this chat is not recommending a routine hormone panel for this concern.

Contact your provider about the concern you reported. Note when you first noticed it, any changes, and questions you want to ask. Do not use a supplement recommendation from this app as a substitute for assessment.

closingLine: Bring this to your provider. I help you ask better questions — your provider makes clinical decisions.
